92:     """
93:     n_ts, sz, d = dataset_sax.shape
94:     seg_sz = original_size // sz
95:     dataset_out = np.zeros((n_ts, original_size, d))
96: 
97:     for i in prange(n_ts):
98:         for t in range(sz):
99:             t0 = t * seg_sz
100:             dataset_out[i, t0 : t0 + seg_sz, :] = breakpoints_middle_[
101:                 dataset_sax[i, t, :]
102:             ]
103:     return dataset_out
104: 
105: 
106: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
107: def cyslopes(dataset, t0):
108:     """Compute slopes.
109: 
110:     Parameters
111:     ----------
112:     dataset : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, d), dtype=float64
113:     t0 : int32
114: 
115:     Returns
116:     -------
117:     dataset_out : array-like, shape=(n_ts, d), dtype=float64
118:     """
119:     n_ts, sz, d = dataset.shape
120:     dataset_out = np.empty((n_ts, d))
121:     vec_t = np.arange(t0, t0 + sz).reshape((-1, 1))
122:     for i in prange(n_ts):
123:         for di in range(d):
124:             with objmode(dataset_out_i_di="float64"):
125:                 dataset_out_i_di = (
126:                     LinearRegression()
127:                     .fit(vec_t, dataset[i, :, di])
128:                     .coef_[0]
129:                 )
130:             dataset_out[i, di] = dataset_out_i_di
131:     return dataset_out
132: 
133: 
134: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
135: def cydist_1d_sax(
136:     sax1, sax2, breakpoints_avg_middle_, breakpoints_slope_middle_, original_size
137: ):
138:     """Compute distance between 1d-SAX representations as defined in [1]_.
139: 
140:     Parameters
141:     ----------
142:     sax1 : array-like, shape=(sz, 2 * d), dtype=float64 (Linux and MacOS) or float32 (Windows)
143:         1d-SAX representation of a time series.
144:     sax2 : array-like, shape=(sz, 2 * d), dtype=float64 (Linux and MacOS) or float32 (Windows)
145:         1d-SAX representation of another time series.
146:     breakpoints_avg_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
147:     breakpoints_slope_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
148:     original_size : int64 (Linux and MacOS) or int32 (Windows)
149:         Length of the original time series.
150: 
151:     Returns
152:     -------
153:     dist_1d_sax : float64
154:         1d-SAX distance.
155: 
156:     Notes
157:     -----
158:     Unlike SAX distance, 1d-SAX distance does not lower bound Euclidean
159:     distance between original time series.
160: 
161:     References
162:     ----------
163:     .. [1] S. Malinowski, T. Guyet, R. Quiniou, R. Tavenard. 1d-SAX: a
164:        Novel Symbolic Representation for Time Series. IDA 2013.
165:     """
166:     sz, d_1d_sax = sax1.shape
167:     assert sz == sax2.shape[0] and d_1d_sax == sax2.shape[1]
168:     s = 0.0
169:     d = d_1d_sax // 2
170:     seg_sz = original_size // sz
171: 
172:     for t in prange(sz):
173:         t0 = t * seg_sz
174:         t_middle = float(t0) + 0.5 * seg_sz
175:         for di in range(d):
176:             avg1 = breakpoints_avg_middle_[sax1[t, di]]
177:             avg2 = breakpoints_avg_middle_[sax2[t, di]]
178:             slope1 = breakpoints_slope_middle_[sax1[t, di + d]]
179:             slope2 = breakpoints_slope_middle_[sax2[t, di + d]]
180:             for tt in range(t0, seg_sz * (t + 1)):
181:                 s += (
182:                     avg1 + slope1 * (tt - t_middle) - (avg2 + slope2 * (tt - t_middle))
183:                 ) ** 2
184:     dist_1d_sax = np.sqrt(s)
185:     return dist_1d_sax
186: 
187: 
188: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
189: def inv_transform_1d_sax(
190:     dataset_sax, breakpoints_avg_middle_, breakpoints_slope_middle_, original_size
191: ):
192:     """Compute time series corresponding to given 1d-SAX representations.
193: 
194:     Parameters
195:     ----------
196:     dataset_sax : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, 2 * d), dtype=float64 (Linux and MacOS) or float32 (Windows)
197:         A dataset of SAX series.
198:     breakpoints_avg_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
199:     breakpoints_slope_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
200:     original_size : int64 (Linux and MacOS) or int32 (Windows)
201:         Length of the original time series.
202: 
203:     Returns
204:     -------
205:     dataset_out : array-like, shape=(n_ts, original_size, d), dtype=float64
206:         A dataset of time series corresponding to the provided
207:             representation.
208:     """
209:     n_ts, sz, d_1d_sax = dataset_sax.shape
210:     d = d_1d_sax // 2
211:     seg_sz = original_size // sz
212:     dataset_out = np.empty((n_ts, original_size, d))
213: 
214:     for i in prange(n_ts):
215:         for t in range(sz):
216:             t0 = t * seg_sz
217:             t_middle = float(t0) + 0.5 * (seg_sz - 1)
218:             for di in range(d):
219:                 avg = breakpoints_avg_middle_[dataset_sax[i, t, di]]
220:                 slope = breakpoints_slope_middle_[dataset_sax[i, t, di + d]]
221:                 for tt in range(t0, seg_sz * (t + 1)):
222:                     dataset_out[i, tt, di] = avg + slope * (tt - t_middle)
223:     return dataset_out
